events.content:
I have created a lightweight reading tracker app that persists books to a local `books.json` file.

### Features
- **Reading Overview (`/`)**: Displays your **Currently Reading** and **Finished** books alongside an **Add a Book** form (title, author, and notes).
- **Mark as Finished**: One-click button to mark any currently-reading book as finished (from the main list or the book's page).
- **Single Book Page & Shareable Link (`/books/:id`)**: Clicking a book opens its dedicated URL showing its title, author, reading status, and your notes (with inline editing and a copyable share link).
- **JSON Persistence (`books.json`)**: All changes are written atomically to `books.json` (configurable via `BOOKS_FILE` env var) so your books remain across restarts without a database.

### How to Run
- Start the app: `npm start` (runs on `http://localhost:3000` by default, or `PORT=<port> npm start`)
- Run tests: `npm test`

### Features
- **Reading Overview (`/`)**: Displays your **Currently Reading** and **Finished** books alongside an **Add a Book** form (title, author, and notes).
- **Mark as Finished**: One-click button to mark any currently-reading book as finished (from the main list or the book's page).
- **Single Book Page & Shareable Link (`/books/:id`)**: Clicking a book opens its dedicated URL showing its title, author, reading status, and your notes (with inline editing and a copyable share link).
- **JSON Persistence (`books.json`)**: All changes are written atomically to `books.json` (configurable via `BOOKS_FILE` env var) so your books remain across restarts without a database.

### How to Run
- Start the app: `npm start` (runs on `http://localhost:3000` by default, or `PORT=<port> npm start`)
- Run tests: `npm test`
